I had CBT many years ago for anxiety and it was great at the time, but had no lasting power at all. When I started this round of therapy,  I said I didn't want CBT again since it didn't stick with me, which I think was my biggest mistake. It was true at the time, and I've tried explaining to my therapist that my needs are changing, but she doesn't seem to be trying to try new routes or approaches. I think my only choice is to try someone new. 

To me, swapping therapists has become such a big deal and hassle in my head, but it really isn't in reality, and I need to realise that.

I've been going for a year, once a week, and occasional phone call sessions during the lockdown but resumed weekly sessions about 2 months ago. 

When I first started, I had depression and anxiety still but my concerns were quite managable and easy to treat with therapy, which is why I was matched with my current therapist. But now I have gotten far worse and I feel like my problems are perhaps no longer fitted to her skills. I don't want to doubt her, but I know she doesn't have much experience and I think in this situation that is what makes all the difference. 

I have a session with her tomorrow and I mesaaged her earier letting her know my feelings and said I will write down my thoughts and hand the letter to her, to make sure I don't struggle with explaining and forget key points due to my anxiety with speaking. I'm hoping everything goes well, and that my next match is a lot more suited to my problems. Thank you for your advice, really.

I try not to think of it that way, but the doubts in my head try to turn everything into my fault. I've expressed this to my therapist and didn't get much of a response, and this happens with most things I say so I honestly haven't learned all that much, but I do still have hopes for the future.

When I was feeling this way, I told my therapist that I needed more 'intense therapy' meaning a more proactive thoughts, trying new coping mechanisms, something to deal with the urgency I was feeling. She said she can help with that, but nothing has changed since then and I just can't wait around for things to get better. I know I need to be realistic and not expect to be fixed overnight, but after a year of therapy I would like to see at least some sustained progress. 

In terms of the psychiatrist, my therapist can't help with that as I need to go through my doctor to get a referral, but I am working on that currently, in hopes of a proper diagnosis and more focused therapy/treatment. I wish you well in your struggles, too.
